newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - South Korean newspapers - June 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Korean newspapers - June 13.

text.p: The following is a summary of major stories in leading South Korean newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy.
- South Korean Red Cross officials kicked off direct deliveries of humanitarian aid packages to three North Korean cities bordering China.

- The Ministry of Finance and Economy unveiled a package of measures aimed at liberalising direct overseas investment and freeing companies from the obligation to finance part of their overseas investment by using their own capital.

- Kim Jong-pil, leader of the opposition United Liberal Democrats, demanded that President Kim Young-sam tell all about his 1992 presidential campaign fund and ask the people to pardon him for the scandal.
- Students at 20 universities expected to withdraw from the radical student group Hanchongryon.
- The Chinese police held eight South Korean news reporters in custody for about two hours for violating their provided coverage rights.
